item.title: Open-source Software and Pipelines for Generalizable and Reproducible EEG Analysis: An Overview
item.description: arXiv:2610.34047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reproducibility, replicability, robustness, and generalizability are essential but distinct requirements for reliable electroencephalography (EEG) research. Achieving these goals remains challenging because EEG datasets vary substantially across acquisition systems, file formats, experimental paradigms, participant populations, event annotations, and recording conditions. In addition, differences in preprocessing choices, software implementations, parameter settings, and computational environments can substantially influence analytical results. This overview examines the standards, open-source software, and computational pipelines that support transparent and generalizable EEG analysis. We discuss the role of the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED), FAIR data principles, and community reporting guidelines in improving data interoperability and reuse. We review major EEG analysis platforms, including Brainstorm, EEGLAB, FieldTrip, MNE-Python, and SPM, as well as automated preprocessing and quality-control pipelines. We also describe supporting infrastructure for dataset validation, curation, standardized event annotation, and scalable cohort-level analysis. Finally, we provide practical recommendations emphasizing standardized data organization, complete reporting of analysis parameters and software environments, code sharing, preregistration, automated quality control, and robustness analyses across plausible pipelines. Together, these practices provide a foundation for EEG findings that are more transparent, reproducible, and generalizable across datasets, laboratories, and analytical tools.

item.title: Retrospective Comparison of Radiation Oncology Patient Message Responses Generated by Epic and Institutionally Managed LLMs
item.description: arXiv:2610.34464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We retrospectively compared Epic-generated draft replies with institutionally managed hybrid GPT-4.1 and Gemini 2.5 Pro responses to 51 selected single-turn radiation oncology messages. Six clinicians, blinded to response source, rated overall quality on a five-point scale and perceived editing effort on a four-point scale. Mixed-effects models accounted for repeated ratings by message and clinician. Adjusted overall-quality means were 2.95 for Epic, 4.27 for hybrid GPT-4.1, and 4.39 for hybrid Gemini 2.5 Pro. Corresponding editing-effort means were 2.38, 1.46, and 1.41, with lower scores indicating less perceived effort. Both hybrid models received more favorable ratings than Epic for both outcomes (all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001), without a statistically significant difference between the hybrid models. These findings support prospective evaluation of clinician-supervised draft generation, though editing time and patient outcomes were not measured, and clinical safety was not established.

item.title: Just-in-time volumetric imaging: Learning 2D-3D thoracic motion models during image-guided interventions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite two decades of innovation, cutting-edge bronchoscopic techniques still fail to yield clear diagnostic decisions in 30% of cases and miss malignancies in 20% of cases. Intraprocedural 3D imaging drastically improves both tool positioning and diagnostic yield. However, each 3D spin represents a static snapshot of an anatomy that is continuously evolving as the patient is ventilated throughout the procedure. Here, we propose just-in-time volumetric imaging, in which a patient-specific 2D--3D motion model is trained on pre-intervention scans before it is needed and then supplies volumetric images from single fluoroscopic projections during sampling. Given the inspiration-hold CBCT already acquired for navigation and an additional motion-inclusive CBCT, our optimization regime named VoxelMap-DualScan (VM-DS), solves a low-rank motion model by alternating least squares and then amortizes it into a projection encoder trained on synthesized projections with known motion, all within a 10-minute window. On eight held-out cases from the public DIR-Lab 4DCT dataset, VM-DS achieved a mean landmark target registration error of 2.8 mm, a structural similarity index of 0.95 and a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 37.6 dB. Accuracy was maintained when reducing the number of projections used for training from 227 to 57. Inference takes 1.5 ms per projection, making the framework suitable for real-time use during image-guided interventions. Code will be made available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap/tree/VM-DS
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Hindley

item.title: Gold nanorods targeting tumor vasculature: Monte Carlo evaluation of the radioenhancement effects
item.description: arXiv:2610.35186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gold nanoparticles targeted to tumor vasculature can raise the dose to endothelial cells, and the enhancement depends on their position relative to the vessel wall. Despite growing interest in endothelial radiosensitization, intravascular and immediate perivascular dose enhancement has not been resolved at the level of individual endothelial cells for different nanoparticle locations. Earlier vascular dosimetry scored thin wall layers, analytic endothelial slabs, or tissue-region averages. This study quantifies the dose enhancement ratio (DER) of gold nanorods (AuNRs) in individual endothelial cells and in the perivascular region for three AuNR locations. Track-structure Monte Carlo simulations in TOPAS modeled a 10 um long, 16 um diameter microvessel segmented into six endothelial cells. AuNRs were placed homogeneously in the lumen, on the inner vessel wall (vascular-targeted), or on the outer vessel wall (extravasated) at concentrations of 5 to 50 mg Au/g water within the vessel volume under 50 and 100 kVp X-rays. All DERs were corrected for the lack of charged-particle equilibrium (CPE) inherent to microscale simulations. Inner wall-attached AuNRs produced the highest microvessel-averaged DERs, reaching approximately 3.8 at 50 mg Au/g water and approximately 1.96 at 18 mg Au/g water under 50 kVp. The DER increased linearly with AuNR concentration and was higher at 50 kVp than at 100 kVp. Including AuNRs outside the simulated segment (infinite vessel approximation) increased endothelial DERs by 5 to 10 percent. In the perivascular region, the DER was highest within the first 10 um, where outer wall-attached AuNRs gave the highest values. The results establish a physical dose enhancement basis for endothelial and perivascular cells and can guide the design of vascular-targeted radiosensitization.

item.title: At last, an explicit singular value decomposition for electrical impedance tomography
item.description: arXiv:2610.35217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a diagonalization of the normal operator of the linearized electrical impedance tomography (EIT) problem on the disk in the case of a radially symmetric Schr\"odinger potential with Dirichlet-to-Neumann data. The diagonalization is achieved by transforming the normal operator to the adjacent interval finite Hilbert transform which has a known spectral theory including a commuting differential operator. The normal operator in this case is not compact and the spectrum continuous.
item.dc:creator: William R B Lionheart, Michael Pidcock, Cristiana Sebu

item.title: End-to-end prostate lesion segmentation and detection from undersampled diffusion-weighted MRI
item.description: arXiv:2610.33554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated prostate lesion detection from diffusion-weighted MR imaging (DWI) conventionally relies on reconstructed images and does not fully use all acquisition information. We present an end-to-end network that uses complex multicoil DWI data and coil sensitivity information for prostate lesion segmentation. We included 269 fastMRI prostate examinations with additional voxel-level lesion annotations. Of these, 64 examinations contained PIRADS 4 or 5 lesions. The proposed network, VarNet-Seg, consists of a k-space variational network (VarNet) with six variational cascades and an image-space 3D segmentation U-Net. Comparator models used the same segmentation architecture with fully coil-combined images (CC-Seg), fixed root-sum-of-squares reconstruction (RSS-Seg), or fixed SENSE reconstruction (SENSE-Seg). We performed ablations with end-to-end training and data consistency (DC) enabled or disabled. We evaluated lesion segmentation using Dice and patient-level detection using AUROC in five-fold cross-validation with full sampling, simulated undersampling, added noise, or both. VarNet-Seg achieved the highest Dice at every undersampling level. At eight-fold acceleration, Dice was 0.22 for VarNet-Seg, 0.14 for SENSE-Seg and 0.16 for VarNet-Seg (no DC). The paired difference from SENSE-Seg was 0.08 (95% CI, 0.04-0.11). With full sampling, VarNet-Seg and RSS-Seg performed similarly (0.40 vs 0.39). Patient-level AUROC decreased from 0.75 with full sampling to 0.63 at eight-fold acceleration; corresponding RSS-Seg AUROCs were 0.76 and 0.64. The proposed multicoil network improved prostate lesion segmentation under simulated undersampling compared to conventional models. Matched ablations supported contributions from both end-to-end training and data consistency. Prospective evaluation is needed to establish whether this approach can be used clinically in accelerated prostate DWI.
item.dc:creator: Lukas T. Rotkopf, Marco Schlimbach, Kevin Kr\"{o}ninger, Stefan O. Schoenberg, Heinz-Peter Schlemmer, Jens Kleesiek, Moritz Rempe

item.title: FlexiMIND: Combined Pretrained Vision Features and Local Structure for Training-Free Deformable Medical Image Registration
item.description: arXiv:2610.34600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Objective. Deformable image registration remains challenging because corresponding anatomy may exhibit different intensity relationships. Hand-crafted modality-robust descriptors such as Modality-Independent Neighborhood Descriptor with Self-Similarity Context (MIND-SSC) and features from pretrained vision encoders provide distinct representations for correspondence estimation, but how they should be combined remains unclear. We investigate whether tighter integration improves registration over a sequential, scale-separated design. Approach. We introduce FlexiMIND, a training-free and label-free two-stage framework in which frozen FlexiCT-2D encoder features establish contextual correspondence and MIND-SSC refines the deformation within ConvexAdam. Five alternative feature-coupling strategies were evaluated under a protocol across CT-CT (DIR-Lab 4DCT 4DCT, 10 cases), MR-MR (ACDC, 50 patients), and MR-CT (Learn2Reg Abdomen MR-CT, 8 pairs) registration. Performance was assessed using target registration error (TRE), Dice similarity coefficient (Dice), SDlogJ, and local folding. Main results. FlexiMIND achieved a TRE of 1.27 mm on DIR-Lab 4DCT, a DSC of 0.807 on ACDC, and an organ-averaged DSC of 0.825 on Abdomen MR-CT. Across 15 coupling-strategy dataset comparisons, only four outperformed the reference method, with a maximum absolute improvement of 0.0043 in Dice, whereas degradation reached 20.6 % in TRE and 37.9 % in Dice. Changes in registration accuracy were closely associated with changes in deformation-field regularity, and strategies that better preserved regularity generally remained closest to the reference performance. Landmark-level analysis showed that the pretrained encoder stage primarily reduced large correspondence errors rather than uniformly improving local precision. Code is available upon acceptance at https://github.com/mosaf/FlexiMIND.
item.dc:creator: Mojtaba Safari, Mingzhe Hu, Shansong Wang, Suyang Xi, Joshua Lorenz, Sean Pitroda, Aytekin Oto, Ralph R. Weichselbaum, Xiaofeng Yang

item.title: High-speed laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina
item.description: arXiv:2610.34605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate real-time laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina using a Phantom S980 streaming camera at $3840\times2160$ pixels, 8-bit depth, and 1000 frames per second, with a $988\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ exposure. We report four recordings of the peripapillary retina around the optic disc in the right eye of one healthy 25-year-old emmetropic man, acquired without pharmacological pupil dilation, using 852-nm diffuse Maxwellian illumination at an entering optical power of 5.0 mW. Each recording contained 4096 frames (4.10 s), and all 16384 frames in the reported recordings were retained. Open-source Holoflow software on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 computes $K=\sigma/\mu$ over $5\times5$ spatial pixels and nonoverlapping blocks of 16 frames, producing 62.5 contrast maps/s with 60-frame/s rendering and no additional averaging. The nominal raw-input throughput is 8.29 Gpixel/s. Main retinal arterial and venous branches and smaller peripapillary vessels were visualized. Variations during the cardiac cycle were visible in the principal retinal arteries and veins, as illustrated in the Supplementary Videos. Regional inverse-contrast traces show an arterial dicrotic notch and spontaneous venous pulsation. This single-volunteer demonstration establishes an operating point for high-throughput retinal speckle-contrast visualization. Physiological observations are descriptive; contrast is an instrument-dependent observable rather than a calibrated blood-flow velocity.
item.dc:creator: Zacharie Auray, Jules Guillou, Basile Malbois, Maxime Boy-Arnould, Michael Atlan

item.title: Bodyseismography (BSG): Theoretical Foundation and Numerical Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.35844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bodyseismography (BSG) records cardiovascular vibrations transmitted through the body and a supporting bed, enabling contactless assessment of cardiac mechanics. Relating these vibrations to hemodynamic features requires separating cardiac excitation from the effects of body and bed transmission. We develop a source-transmission-measurement framework that couples myocardial contraction and vascular recoil to directional BSG observations. The theory connects stroke volume, cardiac output, and blood pressure to observation and target Jacobians, establishes a local first-order target-observability criterion, and characterizes how additional sensing axes reduce ambiguities under specified source and transmission uncertainties. Numerical modeling combines four-chamber cardiac mechanics, cardiac-to-body excitation, and calibrated body-bed operators. Across 27 participants, a multilayer finite-element model with calibrated frequency correction achieves median Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.865 for the vertical channel and 0.682 for the planar-sum channel in matched-window waveform reconstruction. Controlled stroke-volume perturbations show that transmission reshapes feature sensitivity, including a reversal of the vertical feature association in 8 of 27 participant-specific transfer models. These analytical and numerical studies explain how cardiovascular sources and mechanical propagation jointly shape triaxial BSG and provide a physical basis for relating directional vibration features to hemodynamic changes.

item.title: Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations
item.description: arXiv:2602.04375v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Monte Carlo (MC) dose engines are the gold standard for pencil beam scanning proton therapy, but their computational cost limits adaptive workflows and other tasks requiring repeated dose recalculation. Existing deep learning beamlet dose engines require each beamlet to be sampled in its beam's-eye-view, which implies a local resampling of the computed tomography (CT) patch for every beamlet. We propose the Angle-dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm (ADoTA), which adds an input channel encoding a fast analytical beamlet shape projection that supplies the beam direction explicitly. The CT is resampled only once per irradiation field to an isotropic $2\times2\times2$ mm$^3$ grid, and each beamlet is obtained by cropping this shared grid. The model was trained on CT data from 108 patients for initial energies of 70 to 150 MeV (thoracic) and 70 to 270 MeV (abdominal/pelvic) and evaluated on an independent test cohort of 50 patients. ADoTA achieved $\Gamma(1\%,3\,\mathrm{mm},0.1\%)$ pass rates of $99.40\pm0.86\%$ (thoracic) and $99.87\pm0.23\%$ (abdominal/pelvic), with an effective batched throughput of $3.14\pm0.31$ ms per beamlet. In a 5640-spot prostate plan benchmark with both routes optimized on the GPU, the analytical projection reduced the plan's direction-encoding cost by $9.6\times$ and its total compute time by $1.48\times$ compared with local beam's-eye-view sampling. For full treatment plans, $\Gamma(2\%,2\,\mathrm{mm},10\%)$ pass rates averaged 95.1% (lung) and 96.1% (prostate), while the target $D_{98\%}$ was underestimated by 1.8 to 2.5% of prescription in prostate plans and 4.2 to 5.9% in thoracic plans. ADoTA achieves close to MC accuracy at the beamlet level without beamlet-specific resampling, with a clinically relevant target underdosage in thoracic plans that should be resolved before clinical use.
item.dc:creator: Miko{\l}aj Stryja, Danny Lathouwers, Zolt\'an Perk\'o

item.title: Evaluating a Large Language Model for Radiotherapy Patient Scheduling under Realistic Clinical and Operational Constraints: a Feasibility Study
item.description: arXiv:2605.12896v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Radiotherapy scheduling must balance clinical constraints and operational objectives. We evaluated the feasibility of using a large language model (LLM) to generate treatment schedules through simulation and retrospective clinical comparison. A one-year simulation modeled 1,400 new patients across 12 treatment categories and three linear accelerators (LINACs). Structured prompts provided ChatGPT with patient information, schedule status, clinical rules, and operational objectives. Scenarios assessed treatment-time consistency, LINAC continuity, gap reduction, and handling of infeasible requests. LLM schedules were compared with heuristic and constraint programming (CP-SAT) approaches under two objective settings. A six-week retrospective analysis included 2,043 clinical appointments. LLM-generated schedules met all predefined feasibility constraints in the evaluated scenarios, with 98.6-98.8% of fractions within preferred treatment-time windows. Prioritizing LINAC continuity reduced switching from 52.4 +/- 2.6% to 9.4 +/- 0.6%. Gap-constrained temporal relaxation reduced average daily gaps to 47.1 +/- 8.5 minutes and Friday gaps to 89.2 +/- 18.4 minutes while maintaining low overtime. The framework identified predefined violations in infeasible requests and suggested corrective actions. Heuristic and CP-SAT methods also generated feasible schedules, with performance dependent on objective weighting. In retrospective evaluation, all approaches scheduled appointments without overtime; LLM strategies reduced mean gaps by 50.8-77.1% and improved treatment-time consistency from 86.7% to 99.5-99.9%. These findings support further evaluation of structured LLM scheduling as a human-in-the-loop decision-support approach for radiotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Eric Zhang, Youfang Lai, Wen Li, Annette Souranis, Georgia Paparoidamis, Michael Roumeliotis, Xun Jia

item.title: A 2D autocorrelation-based frequency estimator reflecting spatial tissue distribution to improve Ultrasound H-scan tissue characterization
item.description: arXiv:2609.30686v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: H-scan is a promising quantitative ultrasound technique that estimates the frequency content of backscattered signals and maps the estimated frequencies onto a red/blue color scale to reflect underlying tissue properties. Although it relies on matched filters tuned to different frequencies, the broad spectral bandwidth of ultrasound produces noisy, granular displays. Here, we introduce an adaptive frequency estimator designed to suppress the noise within homogeneous regions while preserving sharpness across tissue boundaries. The method combines 2D autocorrelation with a matched filter. In the first stage, a matched-filter-based estimation yields an a priori map of the spatial distribution of frequencies. The local heterogeneity of these estimates then defines a 2D weighting function that guides a second estimation stage. Drawing on the concept of Loupas's blood velocity estimator, we apply autocorrelation over a 2D spatial kernel to recover the axial frequency components, employing a weighted summation that accounts for the spatial frequency distribution within the kernel. We benchmarked the proposed estimator against conventional approaches, including the short-time Fourier transform, the H-scan matched filter, and standard autocorrelation, using both Field II simulations and in vivo data from human subjects with hepatic steatosis. In simulation, our adaptive estimator reduced the noisy texture in homogeneous regions while retaining clear boundary delineation, whereas the other estimators could achieve only one of these objectives. Applied to the in vivo human liver, the estimator improved H-scan image quality by lowering noise and enhancing the discrimination of steatotic liver from adjacent gallbladder and skin layers.
item.dc:creator: Jihye Baek, Thurston Brevett, Dongwoon Hyun, Ahmed El Kaffas, Aya Kamaya, Kevin J. Parker, Jeremy J. Dahl

item.title: Foundation Models in Medical Image Analysis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2510.16973v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advancements in foundation models (FMs) have catalyzed a paradigm shift in medical image analysis. Unlike traditional task-specific artificial intelligence (AI) models, FMs leverage large-scale datasets to learn generalized representations that can be adapted to downstream clinical applications. Despite the rapid proliferation of FM research in medical imaging, there is a lack of unified synthesis that systematically maps the evolution of architectures, training paradigms, and clinical applications across modalities. To address this gap, this review provides a comprehensive and structured synthesis of FMs in medical image analysis by systematically organizing studies into two primary categories: vision-only foundation models (VFMs) and vision-language foundation models (VLFMs), based on their architectural foundations, training strategies, and downstream clinical tasks. A quantitative analysis was conducted on both VFMs and VLFMs to characterize temporal trends in dataset utilization and application domains, along with pooled performance and subgroup analyses. We also critically discuss persistent challenges, including cross-domain generalization, computational scalability, FM evaluation, fairness, and deployment. Finally, we identify key future research directions aimed at enhancing the robustness, interpretability, and clinical integration of FMs, thereby accelerating their translation into real-world medical practice.
item.dc:creator: Praveenbalaji Rajendran, Mojtaba Safari, Wenfeng He, Mingzhe Hu, Shansong Wang, Jun Zhou, Xiaofeng Yang

item.title: Quantifying thermal-signature equivalence in infrared breast thermography using a modified Pennes bioheat model
item.description: arXiv:2605.05713v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Infrared breast thermography measures skin-surface temperature, but heat diffusion and thermal screening can obscure intratumoral physiology. We introduce a tolerance-aware, full-profile framework to determine when distinct intratumoral perfusion patterns become observationally equivalent at the breast surface. We solve a steady-state modified Pennes model for a two-dimensional multilayer breast containing a finite tumor with uniform, rim-enhanced, necrotic-core, or anisotropic perfusion. A conservative finite-difference scheme with a BiCGSTAB solver and an incomplete-LU (IncompleteLUT) preconditioner is verified by mesh refinement and an analytical benchmark. For a representative configuration, equivalent-pair fractions are $2/6$, $5/6$, and $6/6$ at tolerances of $0.020$, $0.050$, and $0.100~^\circ\mathrm{C}$, respectively. Noise tests show that classification depends on how profile-level uncertainty is modeled. Matching tumor-averaged perfusion reduces rim-enhanced--uniform and necrotic-core--uniform profile distances by $97.7\%$ and $99.0\%$, respectively, whereas anisotropic perfusion remains more distinguishable. Greater tumor depth increases thermal-signature equivalence, while larger diameter enhances distinguishability. Among four parameter groups, heat generation has the strongest positive influence on mean profile separation. For fixed representative geometry and perfusion-pattern shapes, a 300-point Latin-hypercube analysis with independent uniform $\pm20\%$ perturbations of these parameter groups finds that about $79\%$ of sampled configurations retain at least one equivalent pair at $\varepsilon_T=0.020~^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Our results show that a detectable static surface anomaly does not uniquely determine its internal perfusion structure.
item.dc:creator: Roni Muslim, Ramacos Fardela, Tista Artu Indra Kusuma
